script.title: Why a Desert Crater Has Been on Fire Since 1971
sentences: A crater nicknamed the Door to Hell has burned since 1971.
It sits in Turkmenistan's Karakum Desert, about 260 kilometres north of Ashgabat.
Hundreds of gas fires light up its floor and rim.
Nobody is sure how it began, because the records are missing or classified.
One account says Soviet engineers drilled there for oil, and the ground collapsed within days.
To stop poisonous gas escaping, they set it on fire on purpose.
They underestimated how much gas was down there.
Infrared images from 2026 show the flames are only now starting to fade.
script.description:
A gas crater in the Karakum Desert has been burning since 1971.
One account says engineers lit it on purpose.
claims_en: The Darvaza gas crater is also known as the Door to Hell.
The crater has been burning since 1971.
It is in the Karakum Desert in Turkmenistan.
It is about 260 kilometres north of Ashgabat.
Hundreds of natural gas fires illuminate the floor and rim of the crater.
Records of the crater's early history are absent, classified or inaccessible, so its early history is still being determined.
One account says Soviet engineers drilled the site in 1971 as an oil field and it collapsed within days.
The engineers chose to flare the crater to prevent the emission of poisonous gases.
They underestimated the volume of the gas.
Infrared images taken in 2026 show the fires are on the decline.
